newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia privatises three more state assets.
newsitem.headline: Zambia privatises three more state assets.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Tuesday it had sold three state assets to local investors.

The latest sales bring to 164 the number of companies and units privatised under a national privatisation programme since 1993. A total number of 275 companies and units have been earmarked for privatisation.

"The Zambia Privatisation Agency is delighted to announce the sale of Mindeco Small Mines Ltd, the Lusaka plant of the Zambia Cold Storage Corp, and Swan Dry Cleaners Ltd," ZPA chief executive Valentine Chitalu told a news conference.

Mindeco Small Mines, comprising the mining license to the Michinga Quarry Mine with estimated limestone reserves of over 55 million tonnes, its processing facilities and offices in Lusaka, was sold as a going concern for 183 million kwacha ($140,000).
The new owners would take over the company's liabilities of 161 million kwacha, Chitalu said.

"In addition to the purchase consideration, it is envisaged that the purchasers will invest a sum equivalent to about $300,000 by way of capital expenditure in the next three years for rehabilitation of the plant and equipment," Chitalu said.
He said the plant, which had the capacity to produce 10,000 tonnes a year, had been producing at 20 percent capacity.
Chitalu said the Zambia Cold Storage Corp plant, whose main line of business includes the procurment, slaughter and processing of livestock, had been sold as a going concern for 850 million kwacha.
It would take over liabilities of 290 million and would invest at least 250 million on plant rehabilitation in the initial year, and a further $600,000 of capital expenditure over five years.
Cleanwell Dry Cleaners was sold for 89 million kwacha.
